trajectory_summary: The call opens cooperatively but the rep reaches a shading disqualification within roughly a minute of a Google Maps glance, without probing roof orientation, sun hours, or the customer's own read of the property. The customer offers two specific, unprompted counter-arguments that go uninvestigated, and the call ends on an unanchored 'I'll give you a callback' with no date or time. Energy leaked from a warm, cooperative start into a customer left contesting a conclusion nobody actually tested.
outcome_dispute: v1 tag is unknown; the observed outcome is best read as a soft/conditional callback, not a clean DQ. The rep never resolves the customer's shading counter-evidence and offers to 'reach out to my design team' and call back 'if they can' — this is a maybe, not a hard disqualification, and it is left completely unanchored (no date, no time, no confirmed next step).

observed_outcome.quote: I can reach out to my design team and see if they would be able to do anything. And then if they can, I'll give you a callback, and we could totally get you scheduled.
observed_outcome.reasoning: The call does not end in a hard DQ delivered with finality nor a booked appointment — it ends with the rep promising to escalate to the design team and call back if the shading issue can be resolved. No date or time is given, making this a callback outcome rather than tentative or booked.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: The call never reached bill collection — it was cut short by the shading DQ discussion before the rep asked about utility company or average bill.

interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep never explicitly asked what interested the customer in solar; the call moved from address confirmation directly into the tree/shading assessment and the interest_question verify item was never reached.

script_coverage.quote: This is Holland with Ion. I got a request that you were looking into solar for your home.
I've got your address here as 1909 McFadden Street in Columbia, South Carolina. Is that correct?

primary_coaching_focus.topic: Premature DQ from a map glance, no verify probing
primary_coaching_focus.quote: So I think that with those trees still there, I don't think that the panels will be able to get enough sun, for them to be super fully fully beneficial to you.
primary_coaching_focus.why: The rep disqualified a warm, cooperative lead off a satellite image in under 90 seconds without asking a single clarifying question about roof orientation, sun hours, or square footage — and then didn't engage with two specific counter-arguments the customer volunteered. This is the single biggest value-destroying moment on the call: a real lead may have been walked away from without being properly assessed.

key_moments.quote: We've only been renting it for about a little over a year, but, we've owned the home for a long time.
key_moments.stewart_read: This answer is genuinely ambiguous on the hard homeowner-verification gate: is the customer currently renting this specific home from someone else, or do they own it and are describing a landlord/tenant history elsewhere? The rep says 'Okay. Very nice.' and moves on without clarifying who is actually on title for THIS address.

key_moments.quote: I don't think that the panels will be able to get enough sun, for them to be super fully fully beneficial to you.
key_moments.stewart_read: The rep reaches a shading disqualification based solely on a Google Maps glance, without asking which side of the roof the trees shade, roof pitch, or square footage available on the unshaded side — verify items that would normally inform this call.

key_moments.quote: But the trees really only only give shade on the portion of the house and only a part of the day, if that makes a difference.
key_moments.stewart_read: The customer supplies a second, more granular counter-argument (partial shade, limited time of day) than their first, and the rep's next line ('It's a ton of space to put panels up there, unfortunately') does not engage with either specific detail raised.

key_moments.quote: So, yeah, I really do apologize, but I can get you off our list if you don't get any more calls. Okay?
key_moments.stewart_read: The rep offers to remove the customer from the call list within seconds of a single map-based observation, before any pushback or further verification — this is a premature exit path being floated on a call that was otherwise going cooperatively.
